title: Nodes
description: Are the machines themselves OK? Open it after a Host* or Thin pool alert, or on a weekly review: CPU, memory, disk, filesystem and network of the Proxmox nodes, the monitoring CT and the k3s VMs.

panels.title: Node exporters up
panels.description: node_exporter scrapes of the selected hosts (rule TargetDown, which covers every job). DOWN means the tiles beside this one are stale: look at Network > Reachability for the host.

targets.expr: min((up{job="node", instance=~"$instance"} or up{job="service_dmz", port="9100", instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.title: CPU temperature, hottest
panels.description: Hottest CPU package among the selected Proxmox nodes (rule HostCpuHot: above 90 C for 10 minutes). Only the three nodes have a CPU sensor; the VMs show n/a. pve1's 20-minute GPU + CPU soak peaked at 89 C.

targets.expr: max(max by (instance) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", instance=~"$instance"} * on (instance, chip) group_left () (node_hwmon_chip_names{job="node", chip_name=~"coretemp|k10temp"} * 0 + 1)))

panels.title: Memory available, lowest
panels.description: Lowest MemAvailable / MemTotal among the selected hosts (rule HostMemoryLow: under 10 % for 15 minutes, nodes and k3s VMs). On the k3s VMs this is the warning before the kubelet evicts tenant pods.

panels.title: Filesystem free, lowest
panels.description: Lowest free-space ratio over every ext4, xfs, zfs, btrfs and vfat mount of the selected hosts (rule HostFilesystemFull: under 15 % for 15 minutes). The Filesystems row names the mount and shows the runway.

panels.title: Failed systemd units
panels.description: Units in the failed state on the selected hosts (rule HostSystemdUnitFailed, 10 minutes). The k3s VMs do not export systemd state and show n/a. The table in the last row names the unit.

panels.title: Clocks not synchronised
panels.description: Hosts whose kernel clock is not NTP-synchronised (rule HostClockUnsynced, 15 minutes, Proxmox nodes). Corosync, TLS and log timestamps all suffer. The rule covers the nodes; this tile counts the VMs too.

panels.title: Shortest uptime
panels.description: Time since the most recently booted selected host started (rule HostRebooted: a node booted in the last 15 minutes, info only). Orange means a reboot just happened: expected after maintenance or a power cut, otherwise find out why.

panels.title: Collector files, oldest
panels.description: Age of the SMART and thin-pool textfile collectors' output (rule HostTextfileCollectorStale: over 1 hour). When these stop, the disk and thin-pool alerts are blind. Only the Proxmox nodes run them.

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over the cores of each host (iowait and steal count as busy). Sustained near 100 means the host is CPU-bound; read it together with load per core and CPU pressure. The monitoring CT's line is pve2's, not the CT's own. No alert rule: the thermal alert is HostCpuHot, in the top row.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: One-minute load average divided by the core count. Above 1 means more runnable or disk-waiting tasks than cores (dashed line). Brief spikes are normal; sustained above 2 is queueing. The monitoring CT reports pve2's load average, divided by the CT's own 2 cores, so its line reads about twice pve2's: ignore it. No alert rule.

panels.title: CPU pressure (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time in which at least one task was ready to run but had no CPU (kernel pressure stall information, 'some'). The direct saturation signal: a few percent is normal, tens of percent sustained is contention. No alert rule.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable / MemTotal per host. The dashed line is the HostMemoryLow threshold (10 %, held 15 minutes). Falling toward it on a k3s VM means tenant pods are about to be evicted; on a node, a guest has grown.

panels.title: Swap in use
panels.description: Swap used per host. A little used swap on a node is normal (idle pages moved out). Growth together with memory pressure means the host is short of RAM. The k3s VMs have no swap and read 0. No alert rule.

panels.title: Memory pressure (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time tasks stalled waiting for memory: 'some' = at least one task, 'full' = all non-idle tasks. The direct saturation signal; anything sustained above a percent or two means reclaim is hurting. No alert rule.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: Processes killed by the kernel out-of-memory killer in each window (the memory error counter). Anything above 0 is an incident: a container or service was killed for lack of memory. No alert rule; k3s tenant limits kill inside cgroups, which this also counts.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time each block device had at least one request in flight (io_time). Near 100 % on a spinning disk means it is saturated; an SSD can be busy and still fast, so read it with latency. The monitoring CT's lines repeat pve2's: the CT sees its host's disks. No alert rule.

panels.title: Disk queue depth
panels.description: Average number of requests waiting or in flight on each device (the weighted io time rate). Above about 1 on a single spinning disk means requests are queueing behind each other. No alert rule.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: Average time per completed read and write, queueing included. Milliseconds is normal for an SSD; a spinning disk is slower (a few ms to tens of ms). Tens of ms on an SSD, or hundreds on a disk, is a stall. A gap means no I/O in that window. No alert rule.

panels.title: I/O pressure (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time tasks stalled waiting for disk I/O: 'some' = at least one task, 'full' = all non-idle tasks. The direct saturation signal for storage: a few percent is normal on a busy node, tens of percent means guests wait on disk. No alert rule.

panels.title: Space and inodes free
panels.description: Free-space ratio of every mount (the HostFilesystemFull rule: red under 15 % for 15 minutes) and, for ext4, the free-inode ratio (no rule: running out of inodes fails writes with space left). The /boot/efi mounts sit near 99 %.

panels.title: Disk runway, days until full
panels.description: Days until each filesystem is full if the last 7 days of change continue (linear, capped at 365). Under 30 days is worth a plan; under 7 is urgent. Mirrors HostFilesystemFull, which fires only at 15 % free, so this warns weeks earlier. A mount that is not shrinking reads 365.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second on each host's physical interface (nic0 on the nodes, eth0 on the CT and VMs; bridges and veth pairs are left out, they repeat the same bytes). Read it against the 1 Gbit/s link (125 MB/s). The WAN-side picture is on the Network boards. No alert rule here.

panels.title: Network errors and drops
panels.description: Packets per second with a hardware or driver error, and packets dropped by the interface (receive and transmit summed). Errors should be 0. All three nodes show a constant 0.1 receive drops/s (one frame every 10 seconds, identical for days): background, not loss. A climb above that means a bad cable, a full ring buffer or a saturated host. No alert rule.

panels.title: Connection tracking used
panels.description: Entries in the kernel connection-tracking table over its limit. At 100 % new connections are dropped (the kernel logs 'table full'). The k3s VMs track the most (every pod connection); the dashed line marks 80 %. The monitoring CT reads 0. No alert rule.

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description: Offset of the kernel clock from its time source, per host. Healthy hosts sit within a millisecond; a staircase or a growing drift means chrony cannot reach its server. The alert (HostClockUnsynced) fires on the sync flag, not on the offset; the top row counts it.

panels.title: Failed units, by name
panels.description: Every unit in the failed state on the selected nodes and the CT (rule HostSystemdUnitFailed, after 10 minutes). Empty is the good state. Fix: systemctl status and journalctl -u on that host, then reset-failed.
